Thanks — reviewed the redlines. A few legal notes and proposed language below (high level):

1) Region commitment: We can include a contractual commitment that "for Acme Health's Production Customer Data, Redwood will process and store such data within the EU (EEA) regions listed in Exhibit B, except where a Customer explicitly instructs Redwood otherwise." That protects both parties and avoids hard-coded absolute restrictions that would block legitimate cross-region failover.

2) Azure-EastUS: We will add Azure-EastUS to Exhibit B as a permitted subprocessor, but tag it as "Non-Production/Test Environments only" for Acme unless Acme signs a separate data-residency waiver. Proposed exhibit line: 
   - Microsoft Azure (Redwood-managed instances) — Roles: Infrastructure/Compute — Regions: EU West (Netherlands), EU North (Sweden); Non-Production: Azure-EastUS (United States).

3) SCCs/UK Addendum: Confirm Redwood provides the EU SCCs (2021) + UK Addendum and will document supplementary measures. We'll attach copies to the DocuSign envelope.

4) Re-execution: Because this is an amendment to Exhibit B post-signature, we'll include an Amendment to the DPA (Amendment No.1) and request e-signature via DocuSign. That amendment will reference the original DPA date and include the updated Exhibit B PDF as an attachment.

Neha — please prepare Exhibit-B-Subprocessors_20260307.pdf with the new lines. Marissa — once you have the exhibit I'll create the DocuSign envelope and route to Acme + internal signers (Legal/Finance).

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
